## Learning goals

By the end of this page:

- I will be able to explain what a Linux distribution is.
- I will be able to choose an edition using hardware, software, support, and user needs.

This is important because the best operating system is the one that fits the computer and the job.

## Choose for the situation

A Linux distribution combines the Linux kernel with system tools, software repositories, an installer, and a desktop environment.

Check:

1. whether the processor and memory meet the distribution's requirements;
2. whether the graphics, wireless, sound, and other hardware work in a live session;
3. whether the required applications are available;
4. whether the release receives security updates for the needed period; and
5. whether the desktop is comfortable for the user.

For this course, use the teacher-approved Linux Mint edition and image. The official guide describes Cinnamon as the full-featured option, MATE as a more traditional option, and Xfce as the lightest option.

[Read the official Linux Mint guide to choosing an edition](https://linuxmint-installation-guide.readthedocs.io/en/latest/choose.html).
